title: Collaborative Whiteboard
summary: Many users editing one shared canvas. The hard part is not drawing — it is that every client holds an optimistic copy of state that must converge, survive disconnects, and reload from durable storage later.

nodes.label: Editor
nodes.notes: Applies every local edit optimistically and renders it before the server has seen it. Waiting for a round trip to draw a stroke would feel broken.

nodes.label: WebSocket Gateway
nodes.notes: Holds the long-lived connections and terminates TLS. Sticky by board, so everyone editing the same board lands on the same session server.

nodes.label: Board Session
nodes.notes: One authoritative process per active board. Serializes incoming ops, assigns each a sequence number, and fans the result out to every subscriber. Being single-writer per board is what makes convergence tractable.

nodes.label: Presence
nodes.notes: Cursors, selections, who is here. High frequency, zero durability — it is correct to drop presence updates under load, and wrong to drop edits.

nodes.label: Fan-out Bus
nodes.notes: Carries ops between gateway instances when a board's subscribers are spread across more than one machine.

nodes.label: Op Log (hot)
nodes.notes: The recent tail of the operation log. A client that drops for ten seconds replays from its last sequence number instead of refetching the whole board.

nodes.label: Board Store
nodes.notes: Board metadata, membership, permissions, and the pointer to the latest snapshot.

nodes.label: Snapshotter
nodes.notes: Periodically folds the op log into a single materialized board state. Without it, opening an old board means replaying every op ever applied to it.

nodes.label: Snapshots + Assets
nodes.notes: Board snapshots plus uploaded images and files. Load = fetch the newest snapshot, then replay the ops recorded after it.

edges.label: ops + presence
edges.notes: One duplex connection carries local edits up and remote edits down. Reconnect resumes from the last acknowledged sequence number.

edges.label: append op
edges.notes: The op is durable enough to acknowledge once it is in the hot log; the snapshot catches up later.

edges.label: asset upload
edges.notes: Images go straight to object storage with a presigned URL; only the reference travels through the realtime path.

flows.label: Apply a remote edit
flows.notes: The loop everything else exists to serve
steps: A local edit is drawn immediately and sent up with a client sequence number.
The gateway forwards it to the board's authoritative session.
The session serializes it, assigns a global sequence number, and appends.
Fan-out to every gateway holding a subscriber for this board.
Each peer applies the op and reconciles against its optimistic copy.

flows.label: Reconnect after a drop
flows.notes: Catch up without a full reload
steps: The client reopens the socket, offering its last acknowledged sequence number.
The gateway routes it back to the board's session.
The session asks the hot log for everything after that sequence.
Ops replay in order and the client is live again — no snapshot fetch needed.

flows.label: Snapshot the board
steps: Ops have accumulated in the hot log since the last snapshot.
The snapshotter drains them and folds them into one board state.
That materialized state is written to object storage.
With the write durable, the snapshotter can record it.
The pointer flips, and older ops become safe to trim.
